tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand this local-first natural-language-to-SQL application and its approval-first operating model. It frames the Streamlit and CLI interfaces, model providers, guarded database execution, and the operational features explored in the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Ways to Run
tour.description: The CLI supports scripts and automation, while the Streamlit application provides the interactive workflow; the Windows launcher makes the latter available with a double click. These entry paths converge on the same safety and execution layers, so choosing an interface does not weaken the approval contract.

tour.title: Runtime Configuration
tour.description: Validated settings establish the selected provider and model, credential lookup, database connection, persistence, and query-warning options before an interaction begins. This central boundary keeps configuration rules consistent across the entry paths from the previous step.
tour.languageLesson: Typed settings centralize environment parsing and validation, so an invalid provider, model, or database option fails at startup rather than during a generated-query workflow.

tour.title: Providers and Pricing
tour.description: The model factory converts the selected settings into a LangChain chat client for the supported local and hosted providers, including Agnes 2.5 Flash with its provider-specific thinking setting. The pricing module keeps dated price rules and special usage modes alongside token-cost calculation, giving every interface a consistent source for budgets and reports.

tour.title: Approval-First Workflow
tour.description: With a configured model in place, the workflow coordinates schema lookup, SQL generation, validation, preflight planning, approved execution, summarization, usage capture, and auditing. Its typed state carries the generated query and approval status through each stage, making an interface action unable to bypass the governed path.

tour.title: SQL Policy Gate
tour.description: Before either database backend sees model output, the validator parses, bounds, normalizes, and checks it against the read-only policy and known schema. This is the central trust boundary: SQL remains untrusted until structural checks produce an approved prepared query.
tour.languageLesson: AST-based validation examines SQL structure instead of relying on keyword filters, enabling single-statement rules, table allow-lists, limits, and backend-specific escape-hatch blocking.

tour.title: SQLite and PostgreSQL
tour.description: The backend protocol gives the workflow common query-plan and runtime-metric value objects, then concrete SQLite and PostgreSQL adapters enforce backend-specific read-only safeguards. SQLite powers the local demo path, while PostgreSQL verifies role and transaction safety before introspection, planning, or execution.

tour.title: Sessions and Privacy
tour.description: The persistence layer stores local sessions, pending approvals, safe messages, configurable pricing, budgets, costs, and run metrics. Privacy-aware audit logging complements it by hashing questions and redacting SQL literals before durable records are written.

tour.title: Costs and Insights
tour.description: The Streamlit page and component layers turn saved state into session resume, cost totals and exports, effective-dated pricing, budget alerts, query plans, runtime trends, and warnings. This makes the operational effect of a provider choice, including Agnes 2.5 Flash, visible after an approved run completes.

tour.title: Evaluation Evidence
tour.description: The evaluation runner executes the JSONL corpus against an agent and measures result quality, safety, latency, usage, cost, and database immutability. It is the repeatable evidence loop for changing prompts, provider integrations, pricing, or backend behavior without relying on manual UI checks alone.

tour.title: Safety Test Suite
tour.description: Focused tests protect the approval workflow, persistence privacy, PostgreSQL role and plan hardening, provider pricing, and parser-backed SQL policy enforcement. Together they preserve the safety assumptions established in the previous layers as the application evolves.

tour.title: Delivery and Change
tour.description: The CI workflow synchronizes the locked environment, runs quality and security checks, tests, audits dependencies, and builds the package. Pre-commit configuration and release documentation then bring those checks and the user-visible changes closer to everyday development and upgrades.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions organize automated checks into triggered workflows, jobs, and ordered steps; local pre-commit hooks move selected feedback earlier in the developer loop.
